Released as the Famicom in Japan on July 15, 1983. Its hardware was based on Nintendo\'s arcade game Donkey Kong.
The day before launch, Nintendo loaded 100 trucks with boxes of Super Famicom consoles. Mode 7 simulated 3D perspective.
Launched in the US with two games, Pilotwings 64 and Super Mario 64. Its controller was the first with a thumbstick as standard.
Nintendo\'s first console with optical discs instead of cartridges. They were proprietary 8 cm MiniDVD-based discs.
Played with a motion-tracking Wii Remote; Wii Sports was a pack-in game. Over 101 million units sold.
Its Joy-Con controllers work as two halves of one gamepad or as separate controllers. Over 155 million shipped by December 2025.
Nintendo\'s first handheld to use ROM cartridges. In North America and Europe it was bundled with Tetris.
Plays Game Boy games too. Pokemon Gold and Silver, made mainly for it, shipped 23 million copies.
It connected to a GameCube with a special link cable. The GBA family sold over 81 million units by June 2010.
Dual Screen, with a touchscreen below. Over 154 million sold with DS Lite and DSi; Nintendo\'s best seller until the Switch.
Shows 3D pictures without special glasses. Less than six months after launch its price fell from US$249.99 to US$169.99.
Sold as the Mega Drive in Japan, the Genesis in North America and, by Samsung, the Super Gam*Boy in South Korea.
Some models had built-in games, including Snail Maze, Alex Kidd in Miracle World and Sonic the Hedgehog.
Sega\'s first handheld. Its backlit full-color screen ran only three to five hours on six AA batteries.
A CD-ROM add-on for the Genesis, designed with JVC. Pioneer and Aiwa put it in licensed home audio products.
A Genesis add-on, made in answer to the Atari Jaguar and in case the Saturn missed 1994. Unveiled at CES in June 1994.
Launched in the US by surprise in May 1995, four months early. It did well in Japan but not in the United States.
Sega\'s last home console, and the first console with a built-in modem for internet access and online play.
Sony began it after a failed venture with Nintendo for a Super Nintendo CD-ROM add-on. Released in Japan on December 3, 1994.
The best-selling console of all time, with over 160 million sold. In Japan its best-selling launch title was a DVD of The Matrix.
Over 80 million sold, the best-selling handheld not made by Nintendo. Its top game is Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories.
A touchscreen at the front and a touchpad on the back. Sony made it from 2011 until March 1, 2019.
At 14 by 14 by 3.5 cm, the smallest major home console ever released. Games came on HuCard cartridges.
Arcade operators could swap game cartridges in one cabinet. Marketed as the first 24-bit system, though its CPU is a 68000.
Plays every game for the black-and-white Neo Geo Pocket, and runs around 40 hours on two AA batteries.
Runs on a single AA battery. The last hardware Gunpei Yokoi worked on before his death in 1997.
An estimated 30 million sold from 1977 to 1992. It shipped with two joysticks and a Combat cartridge, later Pac-Man.
The first handheld with a color LCD, released five months after the Game Boy. Atari published 71 games for it.
Atari\'s Pong in 1972 is recognized as the first successful commercial arcade video game.
Preserving gaming history is its aim; playing the games is \"a nice side effect\". It documents over 32,000 systems.
Based on FinalBurn and old versions of MAME. It emulates Capcom CPS-1, CPS-2, CPS-3, Neo Geo and Sega System 16 boards.

Your library, settings and play time stay in Plumemu\'s own storage on this device, and are never sent. Unless you switch it off (Settings \u203A Advanced \u203A Send usage statistics), Plumemu sends anonymous usage counts and crash reports to the developer from your first launch: country, device model, Android and app versions, which screens and settings you use, how long you play by system. Never game titles, search words or your ScreenScraper account. Crash reports may contain file paths. Switching it off sends one anonymous \u201Cswitched off\u201D count, then nothing. Problem reports are sent only when you press Send in Report a problem, and may contain the log you choose to attach, with file paths. What is sent is kept with no time limit. Once a day on Wi-Fi Plumemu asks plumemu-app.stevensdesk.com whether there is a newer version; Cloudflare, which hosts it, sees your IP address. Switch it off with Check for updates daily, above. With a ScreenScraper account, Plumemu sends ScreenScraper each game\'s file name, size and checksums, and its title when those find nothing, to find box art.
Asks Plumemu\'s update server now whether there is a newer Plumemu. On mobile data Plumemu asks before downloading an update.
